st-qa-money-se-012.text: In the UK, no—earning just above the higher-rate threshold at 40% doesn’t double the tax bill. Most of the extra tax comes from the full 40% bracket once you’re above it.

st-qa-money-se-013.text: Target-date funds that hold other mutual funds typically charge their own expense ratio, but **not** on top of the underlying funds’ ratios—they are usually included in the total cost. The combined expense ratio is the fund’s stated fee, which reflects the entire management layer (including the TTF’s holdings). Some structures may pass through additional fees (like 12b-1 charges) transparently, but standard TTFs treat them as bundled.

st-qa-outdoors-se-009.text: Choose a static rope for **lead climbing** when you’re setting up the route—it’s longer, stronger for static loads, and less prone to stretch. Use dynamic ropes for **bolted lead climbs** or when you need shock absorption for harder falls. Always check the rope’s specific purpose: statics are for fixed anchors, dynamics for active belaying.

*Pro tip:* If you’re buying under €150, check if Amazon UK offers VAT-free shipping (not always automatic).

The first instant of the universe (Planck time, ~10⁻⁴³ seconds) remains untestable because **no unified theory of quantum gravity** exists yet to describe the extreme conditions, though theories like string/M-theory or loop quantum cosmology offer speculative frameworks.

*(Note: Some scientists argue the universe may not have an "origin" if time itself began at the Big Bang, complicating attempts to pinpoint its absolute start.)*

An **ASIC miner** is a specialized hardware chip built only for efficiently solving cryptographic puzzles in mining Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies, like Ethereum post-merge. It’s far more powerful than a regular CPU/GPU because ASICs optimize *only* for hashing, ignoring all other tasks, while general-purpose computers waste energy on unrelated operations.

ASICs beat traditional mining rigs because they’re **faster** (thousands of times), **lower-power** (more efficient), and **cheaper per terahash**—but they’re expensive to produce in small batches and can’t be repurposed.

st-qa-bitcoin-se-013.text: Lightweight SPV wallets only verify transaction headers by trusting full nodes’ signatures of block headers, trusting their longest-chain claim [1]. SPVs are faster but risk trusting faulty nodes [1].
